Title: XML Beautifier
Description: Pretty-print or minify XML in your browser with 2/4-space or tab indent; keeps comments, CDATA and processing instructions and reports parse errors.
Keywords: XML beautifier, XML formatter, pretty print XML, XML minifier, XML validator, format XML online, indent XML
ErrorInvalidXml: Invalid XML. Please check your input.
EditorKeyboardHint: In the editor, Tab indents. Press Esc, then Tab to move focus out.
Seo_Introduction: Turn a one-line or messily indented XML document into a neatly indented tree, or minify it for transport. The browser's own XML parser reads the input, so malformed markup is reported with a line and column instead of being silently “fixed”.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
**Format** puts every element on its own line, indented with 2 spaces, 4 spaces or a tab; an element that contains only text stays on one line (`<to>Ann</to>`), and empty elements are written as `<b/>`. **Compact mode (minify)** removes the whitespace between tags. The XML declaration, comments, `<![CDATA[…]]>` sections, processing instructions such as `<?xml-stylesheet …?>` and the DOCTYPE are kept, and special characters are escaped again on output (`&`, `<`, `"`).

Parsing is strict XML, not HTML: an unclosed or mismatched tag, a missing quote or an undefined entity stops formatting with the parser's message, for example `error on line 1 at column 11: Opening and ending tag mismatch` in Chrome. The internal subset of a DOCTYPE (`<!DOCTYPE x [ … ]>`) is not kept, because the browser does not expose it.

Open a .xml file or drop it onto the editor, then copy the result or save it as `formatted.xml`. The editor highlights tags, attributes and comments, folds elements and stays fast on large files. The indent and compact settings are remembered in this browser; the XML itself is never stored or sent anywhere.
Seo_Examples: **Indent a one-line document**: `AnnBob` with 2 spaces becomes four lines — ``, ` Ann`, ` Bob`, ``. **Keep comments and CDATA**: in `` the declaration and the comment end up on their own lines, and `` stays unchanged inside ``. **Minify**: with Compact mode, an indented `` containing `1` and `` becomes `1`. **Spot a broken tag**: `` is rejected with “Opening and ending tag mismatch: b line 1 and a”.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Add the XML
Paste it into the **Input XML** editor, click **Open** to load a .xml file, or drop the file onto the editor.

### Step 2: Choose the output style
Select the **Indent size** (2 spaces, 4 spaces or Tab) or enable **Compact mode (minify)**.

### Step 3: Format
Click **Format** or press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS). Parse errors appear above the editor.

### Step 4: Use the result
Click **Copy**, or **Save** to download the result as `formatted.xml`.
Seo_Tips:
- Changing the indent or Compact mode re-formats the current document immediately. - Mixed content is split and trimmed: `

Hello world!

` becomes separate lines for `Hello`, `world` and `!`. Don't reformat documents where spaces inside text matter. - HTML habits break XML: `
` without a slash or ` ` without a DTD are errors here. - Click the arrows next to the line numbers to fold elements; Ctrl/Cmd+F searches the whole document. - In the editor Tab inserts indentation; press Esc, then Tab to move focus out. - No upload: the document is processed in the page, which also works offline after the first visit.
